note: Why an answer of the AI is refused, as FACTS, for a text with its markup as the line keeps it. `of` is the judge, in the order the model has always been told: the placeholders (sequence, count, invented), the counts of brackets, the labels, letters added, values run together, then the markup (out of order, emptied, invented). `model_sentence` is what the model is told of one fact: the sentences the checks used to build inline, word for word, since the prompts were measured on the AI. A person reads the product's wording of the same facts (spec/wording.json). Expected values are derived by hand from the written checks, never from the code.

cases.why: same token, same brackets, nothing to say
the sequence first, then each count, then what the source never had; the bracket counts agree (one pair each side)
a model is held to the count over the whole text, a person is not; no label in the source, so no labels fact
a count says THAT a bracket is gone and never which: the label is named once, after the counts
a version number with no word: every token is there once, and a letter appeared between two of them; the pair that has a letter in the source is not judged
a date came back as three values side by side with nothing but spaces: one fact for each pair the source separates with a word
each token is there once, which a count cannot see; the fact names the tokens the model saw (a person is told the game's tags, see game_words); reversed, the pair is not also called emptied
the words the pair styled are gone, and the game would get an empty colour
every tag was lifted before the text left, so a tag in the answer is the model's own
the order is a property: the sentences are sent back in it, and a model reads them in it. The four tokens of the text each hold a pair of brackets, which is why four are expected
two pairs, two faults of two kinds: the order is the one the model has always been told, whichever pair comes first in the text
the judge of a model sees nothing where there should be a line; a screen that shows an answer must not word these for a person (an empty answer is a capture, or a server that refused)
a person never sees the tokens a markup is lifted into: the sentence names the tags the game wrote

in.sentence: ({[!t*0]}) is missing or changed. Keep it exactly as in the source text.

cases.out: ({<b>}) is missing or changed. Keep it exactly as in the source text.
cases.why: the sentence of a person is worded first, then its tokens are put back: whatever surrounds a token stays
a value or a nested string is in the text a person reads, written so
a text without markup has no tag to say

cases.out: the exact sequence "[!v*1]" is missing or altered
cases.why: the sentence of a placeholder fault is the one it has always been
a count of a character of the whole text

cases.out: keep the brackets of "[Att]", "{Hard}" and translate the words inside them
cases.why: the labels named once each, quoted, joined by a comma and a space

cases.out: between [!v*0] and [!v*1] the source has "." and no letter: ".v" adds some
cases.why: names the two values, what the source had and what the answer has

cases.out: between [!v*0] and [!v*1] the source has the word "年": " " leaves the two values side by side — keep a word between them
cases.why: the long dash is the sentence's own

cases.out: [!t*1] closes [!t*0], so it must come after it
cases.why: the model speaks of the tokens it was given, never of the game's tags

cases.out: [!t*0] and [!t*1] surround words in the source: put the translation of those words between them
cases.why: the words themselves are not quoted back: small models copied them into the answer

cases.out: <b> is not in the source: write no tag of your own, only the placeholders
cases.why: the tag as the answer wrote it
